guides.name: Acomptes provisionnels au Québec : quelle méthode choisir
guides.description: Deux gouvernements, deux séries d'acomptes : seuil de 1 800 $, dates du 15 mars au 15 décembre, trois méthodes, intérêts et pénalités, exemple pour 60 000 $.

guides.name: CELIAPP et RAP : utiliser les deux (règles de l'ARC, 2026)
guides.description: Comment le CELIAPP et le Régime d'accession à la propriété (REER) se combinent : 8 000 $ par an, 40 000 $ à vie, retrait admissible, RAP de 60 000 $.

guides.name: Cotisations du travailleur autonome au Québec 2026 (RRQ)
guides.description: Taux et plafonds 2026 du RRQ (12,6 %, maximum 9 791 $), du RQAP (0,764 %) et du Fonds des services de santé, avec la table officielle de Revenu Québec.

guides.name: REER : plafond de déduction 2026 et 2027, date limite
guides.description: Votre plafond REER est 18 % du revenu gagné de l'an dernier, jusqu'à 33 810 $ pour 2026 (35 390 $ pour 2027). Date limite, marge de 2 000 $, impôt de 1 %/mois.

guides.name: Surcotisation au CELI : l'impôt de 1 % par mois (ARC)
guides.description: L'ARC impose 1 % par mois sur le montant excédentaire le plus élevé de chaque mois. Exemples de l'ARC, coût du retard, déclaration RC243 et marche à suivre.

guides.name: FHSA and the Home Buyers' Plan: Using Both (2026)
guides.description: How the FHSA and the RRSP Home Buyers' Plan work together: $8,000 a year, $40,000 lifetime, qualifying withdrawals, the $60,000 HBP and repayment traps.

guides.name: GST/HST Small Supplier Rule for Freelancers ($30,000)
guides.description: Freelancers need not register for GST/HST until taxable revenue passes $30,000. The single-quarter and four-quarter tests, the 29-day deadline and exceptions.

guides.name: How the TFSA Annual Limit Is Set (Table Since 2009)
guides.description: The TFSA limit is $5,000 indexed to inflation, rounded to the nearest $500. Year-by-year table 2009-2026, total room by start year, withdrawals added back.

guides.name: How We Check Our Numbers: 110 Official Figures
guides.description: Our tax calculators are tested against 110 figures from Revenu Québec's published 2026 self-employed tables, with zero differences above $1. How it works.

guides.name: RRSP Deduction Limit Explained: 2026 and 2027 Limits
guides.description: How your RRSP deduction limit is built (18% of last year's earned income, capped), the 2026 and 2027 dollar limits, the March 1 deadline and the $2,000 buffer.

guides.name: Self-Employed CPP in 2026: Both Shares and CPP2
guides.description: Self-employed Canadians pay both halves of CPP: 11.9% on earnings from $3,500 to $74,600, plus 8% CPP2 to $85,000. Worked table and how it is deducted.

guides.name: TFSA Over-Contribution Penalty: the 1% Monthly Tax
guides.description: The CRA taxes excess TFSA amounts at 1% per month on the highest excess in each month. Worked examples, cost-of-delay table, RC243 and what to do first.

guides.name: Estimated Tax Safe Harbors 2026: 90% / 100% / 110%
guides.description: US freelancers avoid the underpayment penalty by paying the smaller of 90% of this year's tax or 100% (110% above $150,000 AGI) of last year's. 2026 due dates.

guides.name: Self-Employment Tax 2026: 15.3% on 92.35% (IRS)
guides.description: US self-employment tax is 15.3% of 92.35% of net profit: 12.4% social security up to $184,500 plus 2.9% Medicare. Worked table at five income levels.

guides.name: Which Tax Instalment Method to Use (CRA, Worked Example)
guides.description: Three CRA tax instalment methods compared in a worked example: no-calculation, prior-year, current-year. Interest, penalties and Quebec's $1,800 rule.
